The density matrix \(\rho = \frac{1}{2}(|0\rangle\langle 0| + |1\rangle\langle 1|) = \frac{I}{2}\) represents the maximally mixed state for a single qubit. In the Bloch sphere representation, any single-qubit state can be written as \(\rho = \frac{1}{2}(I + \vec{r} \cdot \vec{\sigma})\), where \(\vec{r}\) is the Bloch vector. For the maximally mixed state, \(\vec{r} = (0,0,0)\), corresponding to the center of the sphere.
